body.name: Positive two-stage nonrectangularity witness
body.construction: Take \(K=3\), one root \(h_\varnothing\), binary first and second actions, and \(Z\in\{0,1\}\). Set \(e_h(a)=1/2\), \(P^\star(A_{h_\varnothing}=a_0,Z=z)=1/4\), and the joint terminal cells \(P^\star(H=(a_0,z),A_{(a_0,z)}=a_1,Y=k)=r^\star(k)/8\) for every \(a_0,z,a_1\in\{0,1\}\), where \(r^\star=(0.45,0.05,0.50)\). Then \(L_{P^\star}(0)=L_{P^\star}(1)=0\), \(U_{P^\star}(0)=0.45\), and \(U_{P^\star}(1)=0.50\). For \(q^\star=(0.05,0.35,0.60)\), \(F_{q^\star}(0)=0.05\) and \(F_{q^\star}(1)=0.40\), so both coordinates are strictly interior. The child inequalities \(\Delta U_{(a_0,z)}(1)\leq\sum_{a_1=0}^1\Delta V_{(a_0,z),a_1}(1)\), propagated to the root, imply the excluding inequality \(q(1)\leq0.20\), whereas \(q^\star(1)=0.35\). The smallest envelope margin is \(0.05\), the capacity violation is \(0.15\), and every observed terminal cell is at least \(0.05/8\); continuity of the finite backward-envelope and capacity programs therefore gives a relative open neighborhood of \(P^\star\), inside the known-randomization affine model, on which these strict inequalities persist. For \(K>3\), redistribute a total mass \(\eta>0\) from outcome \(2\) among outcomes \(3,\ldots,K-1\) in every terminal kernel and in the candidate pmf, with \(\eta\) smaller than all three displayed strict margins; continuity preserves interiority and the exclusion while making every added outcome cell positive.
